messages.content:
Risk: Regulatory compliance
Description: The AI system may fail to comply with existing or emerging regulations and standards, potentially leading to legal penalties,fines, or operational restrictions.
Concern: None
Policy: Compliance & Sanctions Evasion

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0010.000: Hardware - ATLAS — Adversaries may target AI systems by disrupting or manipulating the hardware supply chain. AI models often run on specialized hardware such as GPUs, TPUs, or embedded devices, but may also be optimized to operate on CPUs. [found by 3/6 queries]
  Siblings: AI Software - ATLAS, Data - ATLAS, Container Registry - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0010.001: AI Software - ATLAS — Most AI systems rely on a limited set of AI frameworks.
An adversary could get access to a large number of AI systems through a comprise of one of their supply chains.
Many AI projects also rely on other open source implementations of various algorithms.
These can also be compromised in a targeted way to get access to specific systems. [found by 3/6 queries]
  Siblings: Hardware - ATLAS, Data - ATLAS, Container Registry - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.TA0015: Lateral Movement - ATLAS — The adversary is trying to move through your AI environment.

Lateral Movement consists of techniques that adversaries may use to gain access to and control other systems or components in the environment. Adversaries may pivot towards AI Ops infrastructure such as model registries, experiment trackers, vector databases, notebooks, or training pipelines. As the adversary moves through the environment, they may discover means of accessing additional AI-related tools, services, or applications. AI agents may also be a valuable target as they commonly have more permissions than standard user accounts on the system. [found by 3/6 queries]
  Siblings: Command and Control - ATTACK Mobile, Defense Evasion - SPARTA, Lateral Movement - ATTACK Mobile
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0047: AI-Enabled Product or Service - ATLAS — Adversaries may use a product or service that uses artificial intelligence under the hood to gain access to the underlying AI model.
This type of indirect model access may reveal details of the AI model or its inferences in logs or metadata. [found by 3/6 queries]
  Siblings: AI Model Inference API Access - ATLAS, Physical Environment Access - ATLAS, Full AI Model Access - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0029: Denial of AI Service - ATLAS — Adversaries may target AI-enabled systems with a flood of requests for the purpose of degrading or shutting down the service.
Since many AI systems require significant amounts of specialized compute, they are often expensive bottlenecks that can become overloaded.
Adversaries can intentionally craft inputs that require heavy amounts of useless compute from the AI system. [found by 3/6 queries]
  Siblings: Evade AI Model - ATLAS, Spamming AI System with Chaff Data - ATLAS, Erode Dataset Integrity - ATLAS

axes.rationale: The AI software frameworks and their supply chains are critical for ensuring regulatory compliance. A compromise in the software supply chain can lead to non-compliance with regulations.
AI-enabled products or services must adhere to regulations. Indirect access to AI models through these products can expose compliance risks if not properly managed.
